rows.name: rupee_count
rows.notes: Rupee count, one byte 0-255, drawn as the top HUD counter (diamond icon) with a two-digit decimal display (X + digit). Found by differential search + write proofs: a 15-byte probe of $0671-$067F showed 13 when $067D=13; load_state then wrote $067D=4 and after 40 idle frames the HUD rupee field showed 4, and $066E=8/$0658=9 showed in the key/bomb fields. Verified by the game's own code: the spend/use routine at PC $6CE5 does DEC $067D (and DEC $067E) when a rupee is spent. Display is event/animation-gated: writing only the byte sometimes needs a HUD redraw to become visible on the top counter. Related bytes: $066D is a scratch that INC/DECs alongside, $067E is decremented with $067D in the same routine.
rows.reference_at_claim: Number of rupees to add | RupeesToAdd

rows.name: key_count
rows.notes: Key count, one byte 0-255, drawn as the middle HUD counter; the icon tile loaded in CHR RAM is a key (bow + toothed shaft). Proof: load_state, wrote $066E=7 -> HUD middle counter showed 7; a second run wrote $066E=8 -> showed 8 (nametable digit tile 8 at row 5 col 13). Corroborated by ROM: the routine at PC $6D3E loads $066E to draw it, and there is a DEC $066E instruction in PRG ROM at offset 0x1527F (using a key).

rows.name: bomb_count
rows.notes: Bomb count, one byte 0-255, drawn as the bottom HUD counter; the icon tile loaded in CHR RAM is a round bomb with a lit fuse. Proof: load_state, wrote $0658=6 -> HUD bottom counter showed 6; a second run wrote $0658=9 -> showed 9 (nametable digit tile 9 at row 6 col 13). Corroborated by ROM: PC $6D46 loads $0658 to draw it, and PRG ROM has STA $0658 at offset 0x4B8F.

rows.name: heart_meter (containers + current hearts)
rows.notes: Link's heart meter, one byte packing both the container count and the current hearts. High nibble = (max/container hearts - 1); low nibble = (whole hearts - 1); the rightmost heart's fill is completed by $0670. Found by differential search: snapshot, take an Octorok hit (3->2 hearts), snapshot -> 144 decreased survivors; a clean single hit on one screen narrowed it to 23; intersecting the two runs left 10, then a fatal hit left 4 candidates ($0439,$043A,$066F,$0670); writing 0x0439/0x043A did nothing, and writing $066F alone changed the HUD, isolating it. PROOF screenshots: $066F=0x22 -> 3 full hearts (baseline); $066F=0x42,$0670=0xFF -> 3 filled + 2 empty outline hearts (5 containers); $066F=0x44,$0670=0xFF -> 5 full hearts. The draw routine at PC $6D0B loads $066F into $0E and $0670 into $0F and calls $6E79, which splits $066F into nibbles (15 - low, 15 - high) to decide the heart count.

rows.name: heart_fraction (fill of the rightmost heart)
rows.notes: Fill amount of the rightmost heart in the meter (the $0670 byte paired with $066F). Discovered by differential search: it decremented along with $066F on every hit (3 hearts 0xFF -> 2 hearts 0xFE -> death 0x00). PROOF: load_state, wrote $066F=0x22 and $0670=0x40 -> screenshot showed 2 full hearts + 1 half heart (2.5); with $0670=0xFF the same $066F gave 3 full hearts. The heart draw routine at PC $6E79 loads this byte into $0F and compares it with #$80: >=0x80 draws the last heart full, nonzero-but-<$80 draws it half, 0 leaves it empty.
